messages.content: Extract the pharmacological entities from this passage of 雷公炮炙論: 凡使甘草，須去頭尾尖處，其頭尾吐人。用酒浸蒸，從巳至午，取出焙乾，細銼用。

drug: 甘草 (Glycyrrhiza sp.) | plant_part: root (頭尾尖處 removed) | process: 酒浸 (wine soaking), 蒸 (steaming, 巳至午 = ~4 h), 焙乾 (roast-drying), 細銼 (fine cutting) | preparation_class: honey/wine-processed root | indication/claim: 頭尾吐人 (the tip and tail cause vomiting - a toxicity warning attached to a plant part) | tradition: tcm | note: the text specifies both a part-exclusion rule and a timed steaming step, so it is a processing-specification passage rather than a simple drug entry.
Extract entities from: 傷寒論 太陽病，頭痛發熱，身疼腰痛，骨節疼痛，惡風，無汗而喘者，麻黃湯主之。麻黃三兩，桂枝二兩，杏仁七十個，甘草一兩。

formula: 麻黃湯 (Ephedra decoction) | ingredients: 麻黃 (Ephedra sinica, stem), 桂枝 (Cinnamomum cassia, twig), 杏仁 (Prunus armeniaca, seed), 甘草 (Glycyrrhiza sp., root) | roles: 麻黃 = 君 (emperor, diaphoretic), 桂枝 = 臣 (minister, assists), 杏仁 = 佐 (assistant, directs qi downward), 甘草 = 使/harmoniser | indication (classical): 太陽病 with 頭痛, 發熱, 身疼, 無汗而喘 | syndrome: wind-cold exterior excess | tradition: tcm | note: quantities are given in classical units - they are historical evidence, not a prescription, and must never be reproduced as dosing.
Extract entities from: 本草綱目 言 黃連 味苦寒，無毒。主熱氣，目痛眥傷泣出，明目，腸澼腹痛下痢，婦人陰中腫痛。久服令人不忘。

drug: 黃連 (Coptis chinensis, rhizome) | properties (四氣五味): 苦, 寒 | toxicity: 無毒 | indications: 熱氣 (heat), 目痛 (eye pain), 腸澼下痢 (dysentery), 婦人陰中腫痛 (gynaecological inflammation) | claimed long-term effect: 久服令人不忘 (memory enhancement) | tradition: tcm | note: the memory claim is the kind of statement that a modern hypothesis generator should flag as low prior - it is repeated in later texts but has no mechanistic anchor in the passage itself.
Extract entities from: 凡藥有十八反：甘草反甘遂、大戟、海藻、芫花；烏頭反半夏、瓜蔞、貝母、白蘞、白及；藜蘆反人參、沙參、丹參、玄參、細辛、芍藥。

rule_system: 十八反 (eighteen antagonisms) | pairs: 甘草 - 甘遂/大戟/海藻/芫花 | 烏頭 - 半夏/瓜蔞/貝母/白蘞/白及 | 藜蘆 - 人參/沙參/丹參/玄參/細辛/芍藥 | entity types: drug_a, drug_b, incompatibility_type=xiangfan (相反) | tradition: tcm | testable implication: each pair is a candidate herb-herb interaction hypothesis; the most mechanistically plausible classes are toxic alkaloid (烏頭/附子) with mucilage-or-saponin drugs, and the most testable screening is CYP/transporter competition plus additive cardiotoxicity. None of this is a dosing statement.
Extract entities from the Caraka Saṃhitā description: harītakī is kaṣāya, madhura and tikta in rasa, uṣṇa in vīrya, madhura in vipāka, and is said to pacify all three doṣas while promoting digestion.

drug: harītakī (Terminalia chebula, fruit) | rasa (taste): kaṣāya (astringent), madhura (sweet), tikta (bitter) | vīrya (potency): uṣṇa (hot) | vipāka (post-digestive effect): madhura (sweet) | doṣa effect: tridoṣa-ghna (pacifies vāta, pitta, kapha) | claimed action: dīpana (kindles digestive fire) | tradition: ayurveda | note: tridoṣa-pacifying is a strong claim in classical theory and therefore a useful target for the theory-predictivity test - if the property vectors are predictive, a tridoṣa drug should be mechanistically broad rather than a single-target agent.

Extract entities from the Canon description of sibr (aloe): it is hot and dry in the second degree, purges yellow bile, cleanses the stomach, and is used for constipation and for wounds when applied topically.

drug: sibr (aloe, Aloe sp., dried leaf latex/gel) | temperament: hot and dry in the second degree (Unani ṭibb) | humoral action: purges yellow bile (cholagogue/purgative) | indications: constipation (internal), wounds (topical) | route distinction: internal vs topical - the text already separates them, which matters because the anthraquinone (purgative) and polysaccharide (wound) fractions are different chemicals | tradition: unani | note: a single 'hot and dry' descriptor is being used for two completely different pharmacological actions; that is a testable weakness of the humoral scheme.
Translate the 炮制 term 酒炙 into modern process chemistry, and say what would be measurable.

Term: 酒炙 (wine-frying). Modern reading: (1) solvent-assisted extraction of moderately polar constituents into a thin film during frying; (2) ethanol-promoted dissolution/esterification of lipophilic compounds at the surface; (3) Maillard and caramelisation reactions between sugars and amino acids at the pan surface. Measurables: loss-on-drying, surface colour (L*a*b*), residual ethanol, HPLC fingerprint shift, and an increase in extractable aglycones vs glycosides. Falsifiable claim: wine-frying increases the extractable fraction of a named compound by X% versus water-frying at the same temperature and time; a controlled comparison with water-frying is the experiment. This is chemistry, not a therapeutic claim.
Translate 煅 (calcination) for mineral and shell drugs into modern terms.

Term: 煅 (calcination, high-temperature roasting of minerals/shells). Modern reading: thermal decomposition and oxidation - carbonates to oxides with CO2 release, hydroxides to oxides with water loss, sulfides oxidised to oxides/sulfates, and organic matter burned off. Measurables: mass loss (TGA), XRD phase transition (e.g. CaCO3 to CaO), BET surface area, and pH/alkalinity of the resulting ash. Falsifiable claim: 煅 converts a carbonate phase to an oxide phase at the quoted temperature, which XRD either shows or does not. Safety-relevant consequence: an oxide-rich ash is far more alkaline and more reactive than the raw mineral, so the modern reading is also a hazard explanation.
Translate 九蒸九晒 (nine steamings and sun-dryings) into modern process chemistry, and explain why repetition could matter.

Term: 九蒸九晒 (nine cycles of steaming then sun-drying). Modern reading: repeated hydrothermal cycling - starch gelatinisation and retrogradation, hydrolysis of glycosides, Maillard browning, and repeated wet-dry surface oxidation. Why repetition matters: each cycle adds a thermal-humidity history and an oxidation window; the endpoint is not one reaction but a cumulative one, and the number nine is likely practical saturation rather than a precise recipe. Measurables: cycle-resolved HPLC/MS fingerprint, colour, residual sugar, and cytotoxicity (for plants such as 何首烏 where the processing is claimed to reduce toxicity). Falsifiable claim: after k cycles the concentration of a named toxic constituent falls below a threshold; the curve of concentration vs k is the experiment, and a flat curve falsifies the processing rationale.
Translate 醋淬 (vinegar quenching) into modern process chemistry.

Term: 醋淬 (quenching a hot calcined material in vinegar). Modern reading: thermal shock (spalling and cracking, increasing surface area) combined with acid dissolution of basic oxides - acetic acid converts oxides/hydroxides into soluble acetates, and carbonate residues release CO2. The result is a more porous, more soluble, often more bioaccessible solid. Measurables: BET surface area, particle size, XRD phase before/after, and the concentration of acetate-soluble metal ions in the quench liquor. Falsifiable claim: vinegar-quenching increases soluble metal content and surface area relative to water-quenching; a water-only control either shows it or does not.
Translate the rasaśāstra term bhasmīkaraṇa into modern process chemistry, for a plant-derived ash such as a triphala bhasma.

Term: bhasmīkaraṇa (incineration to ash, 'bhasma-making'). Modern reading: complete oxidative mineralisation of organic matter, leaving an oxide/ash matrix; repeated grinding with plant juices (e.g. triphala) before re-incineration adds carbonaceous complexation and can convert metal oxides into more reactive forms. Measurables: TGA mass loss to constant weight, XRD of the final phase, particle size (bhasma is specified as extremely fine), and elemental analysis including heavy-metal content. Falsifiable claim: the final product is a defined oxide phase with a defined particle-size distribution, and re-incineration cycles change that phase; XRD and particle sizing test it. Safety: metal-containing bhasmas are a real heavy-metal exposure route and must be screened, not endorsed.
Translate the ayurvedic processing term śodhana into modern process chemistry and explain its role in safety.

Term: śodhana (purification/correction, literally 'making fit'). Modern reading: a pre-treatment that removes or converts toxic constituents - washing with alkaline or acidic media, soaking in herbal juices, boiling, or roasting. Examples: washing/soaking reduces water-soluble irritants and alkaloid content; heating degrades heat-labile toxins. Measurables: concentration of a named toxin before/after (HPLC/MS), cytotoxicity before/after, and elemental analysis for mineral drugs. Falsifiable claim: śodhana reduces a specific toxic constituent by a stated margin without destroying the proposed active; if the toxic constituent is unchanged, the classical rationale fails for that drug. It must not be presented as making an unsafe drug safe.
Critique this hypothesis: 歸經 (channel tropism) data predicts which organ a herb's compounds will accumulate in, because the channels are anatomically the organs.

What is supported: 歸經 is a reproducible textual annotation (the property vector is real, if inconsistent across editions), and it is a genuine, testable prediction - that is the valuable part. What is overreach: the causal sentence. 經絡 'channels' are not the anatomical organs; the mapping is a physiological-relation scheme, and many 歸經 assignments are driven by observed effect rather than by anatomical access. Compound concentration in a tissue is determined by absorption, plasma protein binding, transporters and perfusion, none of which the theory encodes. What would make it a real result: a pre-registered test where 歸經 labels predict measured tissue concentrations or target-family enrichment above a permutation null, with the annotation fixed before analysis. Without that, the hypothesis is a metaphor with a testable shadow. A null result here would be scientifically interesting, not a failure.
Critique: the four natures (四氣 - cold/hot/warm/cool/neutral) predict whether a drug's compounds are thermolabile.

The claim has a real, if loose, chemical intuition: 'hot' drugs are often volatile or irritant (essential oils, pungent compounds) and 'cold' drugs are often polar, ionic or antipyretic-acting. But 四氣 is a sensory-plus-observed-effect category, not a physicochemical measurement, and it is assigned per drug, not per molecule - one plant has dozens of compounds with opposite properties. Thermolability is also an assay parameter (what temperature? what matrix?), and a plant's preparation history already exposes it to heat, so the label and the property are entangled. A defensible version of the study: pre-register the nature labels, measure a defined thermolability endpoint (TGA onset, or recovery after a standard decoction) for purified constituents, and test against a permutation null. Expect low effect size. The likely honest outcome is 'weak association, not predictive', which is still publishable.
Critique: because a plant has the rasa (taste) kaṭu (pungent), its compounds must be volatile lipophilic molecules.

Partially plausible, weakly valid. Pungency is often carried by volatile electrophiles (isothiocyanates, gingerols, capsaicinoids) - so the intuition has chemistry behind it. But the causal direction is inverted: rasa is a human sensory classification of the whole drug, and a plant is typically multi-taste because it is multi-compound. Bitterness (tikta) in particular is dominated by non-volatile alkaloids, iridoids and sesquiterpene lactones, and 'sweet' in Ayurvedic classification includes starchy and mucilaginous materials that are extremely polar. The testable version: does the presence of a kaṭu label predict that the plant's major constituents have logP > 2 and high vapour pressure at 100 °C? That is measurable from structure/constituent tables and can be pre-registered. Expect a positive but weak correlation driven by the pungent families, not a law.
Critique: 十八反 (the eighteen antagonisms) are pharmacological interactions and therefore actionable clinical rules.

The first half is a good hypothesis; the second half is not yet earned. The rule is a pre-modern text-attested constraint, and each pair is a candidate interaction that can be tested (CYP/transporter competition, additive hERG/Nav blockade, chelation, protein binding displacement). But 'actionable clinical rule' requires dose-response data in humans and an adverse-event base rate, neither of which the text gives. Several pairs have known plausibility: 烏頭 (aconitine, Nav activator) with cardiotoxic or mucilaginous drugs, and 海藻 (iodine-rich, thyroid) with 甘草 (corticosteroid-like). Others are almost certainly artefactual or dose-independent. The correct product is a ranked list of testable pairs with a cheap experiment each, plus an explicit admission that absence of evidence is not evidence of safety. Do not convert this into clinical advice.
Critique: the doctrine of signatures - that a plant's shape or colour predicts its medicinal target - is a useful prior for hypothesis generation.

It is a good negative control, not a good prior. The doctrine is unfalsifiable as originally stated (you can always find a resemblance after knowing the use), and it is the textbook definition of confirmation bias - which is exactly why it is worth measuring. The right operationalisation is a pre-registered blinded similarity rating (colour/shape/habitat) of a plant set against known target-organ labels, with a permutation null and a held-out set. If similarity predicts target organ above chance, that is a surprising and reportable finding; if it does not (the expected result), the field gets a clean negative that stops the reasoning being used as evidence. Either way, do not use it as a generative prior without a stated kill criterion.
Critique: Unani hot/cold temperament (mizāj) classes correlate with measured thermolability and volatility of drug constituents.

The intuition is older than chemistry and is not crazy: hot drugs do tend to be volatile and irritant, cold drugs polar and antipyretic, which suggests the classification partly encodes sensory chemistry. The problem is the classification was derived from both sensory properties and observed effects, so it is circular when used to predict chemistry. The tractable study: take the temperament grade (1st-4th degree heat), measure a defined thermolability and volatility endpoint for the main constituents, control for preparation form, and test with a permutation null. Degree of heat is at least ordinal, which makes a monotonic trend test legitimate. Expect a weak positive trend; the honest claim is then 'the humoral grading weakly tracks volatility, not a mechanistic law'.
Critique: 炮制 (processing) is always detoxification, so any processed drug is safer.

False as a universal, valuable as a set of specific claims. Processing sometimes genuinely detoxifies: 附子's diester alkaloids hydrolyse to far less toxic mono/un-esterified forms, and 何首烏's processing is claimed to reduce liver injury. Processing can also *increase* toxicity: 煅 of metals produces reactive oxides and alkaline ash, 醋淬 increases soluble metal content, and overheating can generate new degradation products. Some steps exist for palatability, storage stability, or trade reasons rather than safety. The right product is a per-drug, per-process claim: which constituent changes, by how much, and what the toxicity endpoint does. The falsifiable unit is the comparison of processed vs unprocessed at matched dose and matched constituent exposure - not the generic statement.
Hypothesis: 麻黃湯 relieves 太陽病 by combined bronchodilatation and diaphoresis, and the 甘草 in the formula reduces ephedrine-type toxicity. Design the cheapest experiment that could kill it.

Cheapest decisive test: a component-factorial study in a rodent with 4 groups (full formula, formula minus 甘草, 甘草 alone, vehicle) at matched ephedrine exposure, measuring core temperature, sweat/prep. gland response (or an equivalent thermal endpoint in a non-sweating species) and a cardiac myocarditis marker panel. If the formula-minus-甘草 group shows the same toxicity as the full formula at matched ephedrine exposure, the '甘草 protects' arm is dead and the whole protection hypothesis collapses. If bronchodilatation is unchanged by removing 桂枝/杏仁, the synergy arm is dead. Cost: one rodent cohort, two weeks, standard LC-MS/MS for ephedrine exposure. Kill criterion stated in advance: no difference in any pre-registered endpoint.
Hypothesis: the 甘 (sweet) drugs in the corpus are enriched for compounds that are orally bioavailable, because sweet-tasting constituents survive digestion. Design a kill test.

Pre-register: pick the 甘-labelled drugs with constituent data, extract dominant compounds, compute or look up an oral-bioavailability proxy (e.g. Caco-2 permeability, or a published F% when available), and compare against a matched non-甘 drug set with a permutation null, correcting for tradition and tier. Kill criteria, stated in advance: (a) no separation between the groups' distributions, or (b) the effect disappears once molecular weight and polarity are adjusted for - then 'sweetness predicts bioavailability' is refuted and the real driver is just molecular size/polarity. Cost: curated data plus existing permeability tables, no new wet-lab, a few days. A positive result would need a confirmation set of drugs withheld from the discovery step.
Hypothesis: 煅 (calcination) of shell drugs increases calcium bioaccessibility because it converts carbonate to oxide. Design the kill test.

Kill test is in vitro and cheap: XRD the raw and calcined material (phase conversion either happened or not), then measure dissolved calcium after a standardised simulated gastric digestion at the same total calcium load. Kill criteria: (a) XRD shows no CaCO3-to-CaO conversion at the stated temperature; or (b) dissolved calcium is no higher after calcination at matched total calcium. Either falsifies the bioaccessibility claim, and (a) also falsifies the processing step as described in the text. Cost: one lab day, benchtop XRD plus ICP-OES. If both pass, the remaining question is toxicity/alkalinity, which requires a cell-based GI irritation assay, not a human study.
Hypothesis: 黃連 (Coptis) lowers blood glucose through gut-microbiota-dependent AMPK activation rather than systemic absorption. Design the kill test.

Three-arm test in a diet-induced obesity mouse model: berberine orally, berberine with an antibiotic microbiota-depletion cocktail, vehicle; plus germ-free vs conventionalised animals. Kill criteria in advance: (a) if antibiotic depletion does not reduce the metabolic effect, the microbiota-dependence claim is dead; (b) if plasma berberine concentrations do not reach a level that activates AMPK in cells, the systemic-AMPK arm is dead; (c) if faecal transplant from berberine-treated animals does not transfer the phenotype, the causal microbiota claim is dead. Cost: one mouse cohort, 8-10 weeks. This is the design that separates the 'microbiota drug' hypothesis from the trivial 'systemic drug' one.
Hypothesis: the tridoṣa-pacifying claim (vāta, pitta, kapha all reduced) predicts that a drug will act on multiple independent targets rather than one, and this is measurable. Design the kill test.

Define the operational prediction first: a tridoṣa-labelled drug should hit >= 2 mechanistically independent target classes in an unbiased target-deconvolution panel (e.g. kinase + GPCR + ion-channel panels), more often than a single-doṣa-labelled drug. Kill criteria: (a) no difference in the number of independent target classes between the two label groups; (b) any apparent difference vanishes after controlling for number of constituents and study effort. Cost: existing commercial target panels on a modest compound set plus the curated labels, roughly a few thousand euros and a month. A positive result would need an out-of-sample confirmation set, and 'multiple targets' is a liability as much as an opportunity.
Hypothesis: vīrya (hot vs cold potency) predicts thermolability of a drug's active constituents. Design the kill test.

Operationalise vīrya as the classical hot/cold label, thermolability as the fraction of a named major constituent recovered after a standardised 100 °C, 60-min aqueous extraction (or a TGA onset for purified compounds). Pre-register the drug set and the constituent list before measuring. Kill criteria: (a) no separation between hot- and cold-labelled distributions; or (b) the separation disappears after adjusting for whether the drug is aromatic/volatile (which overlaps with the hot label); then the claim is a tautology, not a prediction. Cost: existing analytical chemistry, no animal work, about two weeks. Independent test would use purified constituents with a computed boiling point/volatility proxy.
Hypothesis: drugs graded 'hot in the second degree' are enriched for TRPV1 agonists. Design the kill test.

Pre-register the temperament grades, then run the dominant constituents through a TRPV1 calcium-flux assay with a capsaicin positive control and a ruthenium-red/vehicle negative control. Kill criteria: (a) no enrichment of TRPV1 agonism in the hot-second-degree set versus a matched neutral set; (b) activity only at concentrations above the plant's achievable exposure (use decoction concentrations as the ceiling); (c) loss of signal with an orthogonal FLIPR/second-messenger assay, indicating a fluorescent artefact. Cost: one 96-well plate campaign plus the curated labels, days to weeks. A positive result would be a genuine theory-to-pharmacology hit and deserves an out-of-sample set; the likely outcome is a modest enrichment limited to the pungent families.
Extract entities from: 金匱要略 治 痰飲 病，胸脅支滿，目眩，苓桂術甘湯主之。茯苓、桂枝、白朮、甘草。

formula: 苓桂術甘湯 (Poria-Cassia-Atractylodes-Licorice decoction) | ingredients: 茯苓 (Poria cocos, sclerotium), 桂枝 (Cinnamomum cassia, twig), 白朮 (Atractylodes macrocephala, rhizome), 甘草 (Glycyrrhiza sp., root) | indication (classical): 痰飲 with 胸脅支滿 (chest/hypochondrial fullness) and 目眩 (dizziness) | roles: 茯苓 君 (drains damp), 桂枝 臣 (warms and transforms), 白朮 佐 (strengthens spleen), 甘草 使 (harmonises) | tradition: tcm | note: 'dampness' has no modern equivalent; the mechanistically reachable reading is fluid handling, which is why the Poria/pachymic-acid hypothesis is worth testing separately.
Extract entities from: 本草經集注 云 人參 味甘微寒，主補五臟，安精神，定魂魄，止驚悸，除邪氣，明目，開心益智。

drug: 人參 (Panax ginseng, root) | properties: 甘, 微寒 | claimed actions: 補五臟 (tonify the five organs), 安精神 (calm the spirit), 定魂魄 (stabilise hun-po), 止驚悸 (stop palpitations), 開心益智 (open the heart and improve cognition) | entity types: drug, property, indication (cognitive, cardiac, psychological) | tradition: tcm | note: the cognitive claim has a modern ginsenoside/Rg1 hypothesis attached, but the classical claim is broad and partially confounded with general tonic effects - the falsifiable unit is a specific compound on a specific cognitive endpoint.
Extract entities from this Suśruta Saṃhitā line (translation): the bitter, astringent drugs with uṣṇa vīrya are used to scrape away aggravated kapha when the channels are obstructed.

doṣa: kapha (aggravated) | rasa: tikta (bitter), kaṣāya (astringent) | vīrya: uṣṇa (hot) | action: 'scraping' (lekhana) - reducing obstruction / reducing bulk | entity types: doṣa, rasa, vīrya, action, indication (channel obstruction) | tradition: ayurveda | note: 'scraping' is a therapeutic action term, not a molecule; modern translation candidates are lipolysis, mucolysis or reduced tissue oedema, each with different assays. The text gives a decision rule, not a mechanism - so it limits what hypotheses are justified.
Translate 蜜炙 (honey-frying) into modern process chemistry and list the confound it introduces for pharmacology.

Term: 蜜炙 (honey-frying). Modern reading: sugar (fructose/glucose)-driven Maillard browning and caramelisation at the herb surface, mild thermal degradation, and a physical coating that slows extraction at the start of decoction. Confound: honey is itself pharmacologically active (osmotic, antimicrobial, phenolic, and a sugar load that changes gut microbiota), so a 'honey-fried herb works better' study cannot attribute the effect to the herb unless it includes a honey-alone arm. Measurables: 5-HMF and colour (Maillard markers), sugar content, extract kinetics, and a honey-alone control. Falsifiable claim: honey-frying changes the extraction profile of named compounds in a way not reproduced by adding honey after the preparation - a clean, cheap experiment.
Translate 炒炭 (frying to charcoal) into modern process chemistry and note the safety trade-off.

Term: 炒炭 (frying until the surface blackens into charcoal). Modern reading: partial pyrolysis - dehydration, decarboxylation, formation of polycyclic aromatic structures, and loss of volatile constituents; surface charcoal and residual original material coexist. Safety trade-off: pyrolysis can destroy a toxic constituent (the intended effect for some drugs) but also generates PAHs and loss of the presumed active; the product is chemically heterogeneous and batch-dependent. Measurables: mass loss, PAH panel (GC-MS), residual toxic constituent, and carbon content (elemental analysis). Falsifiable claim: the process reduces a named toxic constituent substantially while retaining most of a named active - if both fall together, the process is just destroying the drug, and the claim fails.
Critique: the 君臣佐使 (emperor/minister/assistant/courier) hierarchy in a formula can be recovered statistically from ingredient co-occurrence networks, and a recovered role predicts mechanism.

The first half is a real, doable study: formula-role labels are text-attested for many formulas and co-occurrence network position is computable, so you can test whether role correlates with centrality, dose share, or interaction degree. The second half is where it usually breaks: 'courier' (使) is often assigned to a low-dose ingredient thought to direct the action, and directing action is a hypothesis about pharmacokinetics (permeation enhancement, transporter inhibition) or organ targeting - it must be tested as PK, not inferred from network position. A defensible design pre-registers the role labels, derives network metrics blind to them, and tests whether 使-role ingredients are enriched for known PK-modifiers (e.g. piperine-type CYP/P-gp inhibitors). Kill criterion: no enrichment after controlling for dose share. Without that, the statistical recovery and the mechanistic claim are independent and the second is not supported.
Extract entities and the incompatibility rule from: 十九畏 - 硫黃畏朴硝，水銀畏砒霜，狼毒畏密陀僧，巴豆畏牽牛，丁香畏鬱金，川烏、草烏畏犀角，牙硝畏三稜，官桂畏石脂，人參畏五靈脂。

rule_system: 十九畏 (nineteen mutual fears) | pairs: 硫黃-朴硝 | 水銀-砒霜 | 狼毒-密陀僧 | 巴豆-牽牛 | 丁香-鬱金 | 川烏/草烏-犀角 | 牙硝-三稜 | 官桂-石脂 | 人參-五靈脂 | relation type: xiangwei (相畏, mutual fear) | entity classes: mineral + mineral (硫黃/朴硝, 水銀/砒霜), mineral + plant, plant + plant | tradition: tcm | testable note: the mineral-mineral pairs are the most chemically tractable (precipitation, redox, complexation); the plant-plant pairs are more likely to be PK or additive-toxicity interactions.犀角 is from a CITES-protected species and must be treated as a conservation/heritage issue, never sourced.
